ranking_rationale: The top traces kept their factual claims tied to dated items in their own bank, handled the seasonal mismatch between winter-2026 headlines and a June return either by discounting it (principle_memory) or by not invoking it at all (factor_memory), and connected their probability mass to where their estimate sat relative to the two boundaries. The bottom traces either asserted something and then leaned on its negation - hgf calling the intervals unavailable and then using them, structure_memory reversing its own upside and downside mass between blocks, direct_forecast recording two different predictions - or, in direct_forecast's case, offered no question-specific content at all.
shared_evidence_note: All seven landed on 'within recent range', so the split was not caused by the different banks: the two E1 methods leaned bearish off April/May futures-sentiment and supply items that E0 lacks while the E0 methods weighed EIA revision headlines, but the real separation came from reasoning discipline - whether a January freeze was allowed to speak for a June return, and whether the probability mass was argued or simply restated between blocks.
